A clean parry input (forward, then back to neutral within 6 frames) has a 10 frame window, so 1/6th of a second.
but it's not cancelable into another parry like in SFV, right? So the link should be 4 links which is pretty tight.

After a successful parry you have 2 frames where you will auto-parry any other attack, and some frames of recovery which can be cancelled into another parry or a throw tech attempt.

The gaps between hits in Chun's Super are pretty tight, but the parry freeze makes it a bit easier, and the rhythm is pretty consistent. Once you land the first parry the rest is muscle memory.

It was an individual high-parry each time the kick came. Just as Farseli mentioned, blocking would have killed Daigo. As for how it was accomplished, you basically have to time your forward-taps so that you're doing each time you're attacked. If he had held the back direction, he would have blocked and been defeated. In addition, he had to keep within range to pull this off which meant moving forward into the attack, which you can see halfway through Justins' super. More than just reaction speed, you have to be so familiar with the game that you can pull something of this caliber off reliably. Parries, guard breaks, etc are upper level stuff if you can do it regularly.

As a follow up, given the fact that Daigo would have died instantly had even one of these kicks landed, he was under intense pressure to win since both players had won a round. It isn't just the fact that he parried, he came back from a sliver of health and managed to parry every single kick, knowing that if he missed once it would be game over for him. He did this while there was massive cheering in the background. Everyone was watching. I remember seeing this in college back in 04. Even now, I get shivers because I know that I'll never see something so intense in gaming ever again. I may witness massive space battles, I may watch an intense comeback in a MOBA, I may even see a fighter game battle which rivals this, but nothing will be as intense as this fight, which won Daigo this fight.

Additionally, he had to predict when Justin was going to super, as he needs to start parrying (tapping forward) before the super freeze happens. You can see this happening when they are dancing around mid-screen and Daigo is doing small forward movements periodically. If he presses forward and doesn't parry anything, he can't parry again for another half-second and is completely vulnerable. Justin is scared of this and fakes the super a couple of times before actually doing it, but Daigo predicts this and times the parry well.

Once he has the first parry the rest is set, if he has practiced it enough.

And they are on regular timers, mega every 35 second (but on this map every minute 30) and red every :25 seconds. So it's important for everyone to time when items will be up (IN THEIR HEAD) and know when your enemy has stolen one etc. so you know how much health they will have in a fight and whether or not you're higher or lower than they are etc. etc.

So with the power off, these guys decide to play out the last 28 seconds of the game, and remember how to go and pick up the items and what their health/armor stacks were when the power went out, go through the map and 'replay' the entire match, getting armor and items to remember where they were, and then pause it again at 28 seconds left to finish the map -- with Cooller in the lead and a great stack and the assumption that Strenx will be losing. And of course, the way things go is epic.

Setup: Loser's bracket final between Daigo(Ryu) and Justin(Chun-Li). Both players have one victory, so whoever wins this match takes 2nd place.

Important gameplay information: normally blocking causes you to still take damage(albeit greatly reduced and of course you don't flinch) but if you time it just right, you take no damage. This is called a parry(as opposed to just "block"). Furthermore, to prevent parry abuse, after letting go of block you cannot block again for half a second - otherwise you could just spam the block button and parry everything.

Daigo is reduced to a sliver of health(on the video you can't even see it!), and basically any damage at all from Justin - even blocked damage - will end him. Justin tries to bait Daigo into blocking to take advantage of that half second block delay, but he doesn't fall for it - this is the "dancing" that happens at around 30 second mark. Finally, Justin goes in with the combo, but Daigo proceeds to parry every single hit of it(I think that's 15 hits) including moving in between the different legs(otherwise he'd be pushed out of the combo and wouldn't be able to parry anymore) and the jump parry at the end. Then he counterattacks with his own combo, getting Justin from 40% health to 0.

Each of these parries had to be executed in a <100ms window. I couldn't find the exact value, sadly.
